Name: Adult Platinum Dragon
Source: Lyres Guide to Risk and Reward
Information:
**Platinum Dragons** 

A special, rare breed of metallic dragon that serves as the pinnacle of its kind, and embodies good-aligned dragons.

In times long since past, Platinum dragons were the rarest of their kind. The Old World worshiped one as a god and mostly believed only one existed, but this proved untrue. With the fall of the first Cosmic Teardrop and reshaping of the world, platinum dragons emerged into the world from their places of eternal hiding.

Platinum dragons are notable in that they feature no wings. Their bodies are held aloft by supernatural means, floating and twisting through the air majestically without the need for them. When hanging in the air they can achieve an almost unnatural stillness.

***Inheritors of Justice.*** Platinum dragons are born with an innate sense of cosmic justice. Not necessarily aligned with the morals of men, they desire peace and retribution for all those who were done wrong and preyed upon. They protect communities and innocent life surrounding their lairs, and have a soft spot for mortal beings aspiring to just ideals. However, as they see things from the perspective of a dragon with eternal life, their sense of justice sometimes conflicts with the justice of mortal men.

***Platinum Hoards.*** Platinum dragons predictably covet that which matches their scales. They desire platinum coins, art objects, weapons and more. As they don’t believe in theft, they will often take on a mortal disguise and offer their services to others in exchange for the objects and materials they desire, leading to there being many heroes who were secretly platinum dragons satiating their appetite. Given the rarity of their dietary needs, they temper their hunger and eat rarely (apart from consuming meat and regular food).

When communities desire the aid of a platinum dragon, they will find that gifts of platinum and silver win them over. However, they will not take tribute that was unlawfully taken from others, and have even been known to give parts of their own hoard to communities devastated by tyranny and greed to get them back on their feet.

***Bound by Morality.*** These dragons are heroic and believe in justice, but due to their adherence to their own morality they can be seen as absolute and unmoving by others. Metallic dragons will often heed their advice, but adventurers and dragon-kind alike will often find a platinum dragon entirely unwilling to budge on their stance if they feel something is important enough to stand up for. They will go as far as to fight dragons and heroes to the death if they believe it is in the interest of balance and justice.

“Old World ruins speak of platinum dragons as truly rare - as though the number alive could be counted on one hand. I wonder if those we know of in our modern world are related to them or if our platinum dragons are a different breed entirely. That’s generous to the ruins, though: the Old World’s records are rarely consistent.”

***A Platinum Dragon’s Lair.*** A platinum dragon’s lair is usually not hidden from those brave enough to reach it. They construct strongholds with large halls and quarters where they might hold meetings with dragons and mortals. They are somewhat pompous, and so paintings and statues featuring them adorn their homes. They enjoy lairs that are open to the sun and stars, which they take pleasure basking in.

***Regional Effects.*** The region surrounding a platinum dragon’s lair is warped and altered by their magical influence, which creates one or more of the following effects:

• Platinum and silver within 5 miles of their lair become comfortably warm to the touch, and seem to weigh half as much as they would otherwise. These coins and armor, as well as religious symbols of lawful gods, slowly repair and clean themselves, restoring scratches, nicks, snuffs, and their metallic coatings become reflective.
• Bodies of water within 1 mile become so still they can be used as mirrors, and the water takes on a slightly metallic appearance. If touched, this water eases pain and refreshes the skin. Burns and cuts are restored, allowing creatures to regain 2d8 hit points for every 10 minutes they spend treating their body with this platinum water.
• Creatures observing the sky and stars from within 5 miles will see shimmering rainbow lights dancing in the sky, softly twisting and bending starlight to make the night sky brilliant and inviting. Creatures will find that they can see at night as long as the stars are out as if there was still bright light, but this light isn’t so intense that it prevents sleep or bothers one’s eyes.
• Lawful and good creatures who attempt to sleep within 10 miles of the dragon’s lair find it remarkably easy to do so, but also retain their full passive Perception while asleep as if keeping watch. While dreaming, a platinum dragon may choose to affect a creature as though by the dream spell to converse with them, or may pull their spirit out of their body as by the dream walk spell and appear to them in a spirit form they choose (causing neither any pain or damage when they return to their bodies).

If the dragon dies, these effects end immediately.

traits.name: Innate Spellcasting
traits.description: The dragon’s spellcasting ability is Charisma. It can cast the following spells, requiring no components:

traits.name: Unusual Nature
traits.description: The dragon does not have to breathe and can live normally in a vacuum.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The dragon uses its Enrapturing Presence, then makes three weapon attacks: one with its Bite and two with its Claws.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. Hit: 18 (2d10 + 8) piercing damage plus 6 (1d10) radiant damage.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 17 (2d8 + 8) slashing damage.

actions.name: Tail
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +14 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. Hit: 19 (2d10 + 8) slashing damage.

actions.name: Enrapturing Presence
actions.description: Each creature of the dragon’s choice within 120 feet of it that is aware of it must succeed a DC 22 Charisma saving throw or be charmed for 1 round (until the start of the dragon’s next turn). If the dragon deals damage to the creature during this period or takes an action that is directly harmful to it, it can reattempt the saving throw with advantage. If a creature succeeds either save, it becomes immune to the dragon’s Enrapturing Presence for the next 24 hours.

actions.name: Breath Weapon (Recharge 5-6)
actions.description: The dragon uses one of the following breath weapon options:

options.name: Radiant Breath
options.description: The dragon exhales a torrent of radiant rainbow energy in a 60-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 21 Dexterity saving throw, taking 77 (14d10) radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

options.name: Blinding Flare
options.description: The dragon charges blinding radiant energy and blasts it at a point it can see within 120 feet, where it explodes in a 30-foot-radius sphere. Each creature in that area must make a DC 21 Constitution saving throw, and on a failed save is blinded for 1 minute and takes 14 (4d6) radiant damage. Creatures blinded this way can reattempt the saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success.

bonus_actions.name: Change Shape
bonus_actions.description: The dragon transforms into any creature that is Medium, Small or Tiny, while retaining its game statistics (other than its size), though if it is Tiny it cannot use its Multiattack. This transformation ends if the dragon is reduced to 0 hit points or uses a bonus action to end it.

options.name: Detect
options.description: The dragon makes a Wisdom (Perception) check.

options.name: Attack
options.description: The dragon makes a Claw attack.

options.name: Blinding Gleam
options.description: All creatures within 15 feet of the dragon are subjected to a dazzling flash from the dragon’s scales and must succeed a DC 21 Constitution saving throw, or be blinded until the end of the dragon’s next turn.

lair_actions.intro: On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the dragon takes a lair action to cause one of the following effects; the dragon can’t use the same effect two rounds in a row:

options.name: Radiant Spears
options.description: Lances of radiant energy launch at up to three creatures within 60 feet of the dragon. Each must succeed a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw, taking 21 (6d6) radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

options.name: Planar Void
options.description: Three creatures the dragon can see within 120 feet of it must succeed a DC 16 Charisma saving throw or be banished to a demiplane, itself housed within the plane of positive energy. Once within the plane they are blinded, all magical effects the creature is benefiting from that have a duration end immediately, and any temporary hit points they have vanish. The creature repeats the Charisma saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect and returning on a success. When a creature returns it reappears in the space it left from, or in the closest unoccupied space to it if its original space is occupied. This effect ends if the dragon takes another lair action, in which case the creatures reappear.

options.name: Enfeebling Aura
options.description: All creatures the dragon chooses within 120 feet of it must succeed a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw. If they fail, every time they roll an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw until initiative count 20 the following round, they roll 1d4 and subtract it from the result.
